claim: Novel single-cell-based technologies hold the promise of matching T cell receptor (TCR) sequences with their cognate peptide-MHC recognition motif in a high-throughput manner.
source: Novel single-cell-based technologies hold the promise of matching T cell receptor (TCR) sequences with their cognate peptide-MHC recognition motif in a high-throughput manner.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of single-cell technologies, supported by the context of the manuscript and general knowledge in the field.

claim: Parallel capture of TCR transcripts and peptide-MHC is enabled through the use of reagents labeled with DNA barcodes.
source: Parallel capture of TCR transcripts and peptide-MHC is enabled through the use of reagents labeled with DNA barcodes.
evidence: This describes the technical approach used in the study, which is demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: Analysis and annotation of single-cell sequencing (SCseq) data are challenged by dropout, random noise, and other technical artifacts.
source: However, analysis and annotation of such single-cell sequencing (SCseq) data are challenged by dropout, random noise, and other technical artifacts that must be carefully handled in the downstream processing steps.
evidence: This is supported by the detailed analysis of noise and artifacts presented in the Results section and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: ITRAP (improved T cell Receptor Antigen Paring) is a rational, data-driven method to filter single-cell data and enable generation of large sets of TCR-pMHC sequence data.
source: We here propose a rational, data-driven method termed ITRAP (improved T cell Receptor Antigen Paring) to deal with these challenges, filtering away likely artifacts, and enable the generation of large sets of TCR-pMHC sequence data with a high degree of specificity and sensitivity, thus outputting the most likely pMHC target per T cell.
evidence: This is the main methodological contribution of the paper, validated through multiple performance metrics presented in the Results section.

claim: The ITRAP approach was validated across 10 different virus-specific T cell responses in 16 healthy donors.
source: We have validated this approach across 10 different virus-specific T cell responses in 16 healthy donors.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Up to 1494 high-confident TCR-pMHC pairs were identified from 4135 single cells.
source: Across these samples, we have identified up to 1494 high-confident TCR-pMHC pairs derived from 4135 single cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study, presented in the abstract and supported by data in the Results section.

claim: T cells are essential for immune protection and play a critical role in the immune response to pathogens or cancer.
source: T cells are essential for immune protection and play a critical role in the immune response to pathogens or cancer, where they directly kill infected or malignant host cells or orchestrate the response of other immune cells.
evidence: This is established immunological knowledge cited in the introduction.

claim: Recognition of antigens by T cells is mediated through the heterodimeric T-cell receptor (TCR) which engages specifically with a peptide antigen displayed in the MHC.
source: Recognition is mediated through the heterodimeric T-cell receptor (TCR) expressed on the surface of T cells, which engages specifically with a peptide antigen (p) displayed in the MHC.
evidence: This is fundamental immunological knowledge about TCR-pMHC interactions.

claim: Accurate specificity and broad coverage of antigen recognition are obtained through somatic recombination of the genetic loci, V(D)J, that encodes the α (VJ) and β (VDJ) chains of TCR.
source: Accurate specificity and broad coverage of antigen recognition are obtained through somatic recombination of the genetic loci, V(D)J, that encodes the α (VJ) and β (VDJ) chains of TCR.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TCR diversity generation.

claim: An estimated 10^7 distinct αβTCRs exist in an individual.
source: The process creates an extensively variable and dynamic repertoire, with an estimated 107 distinct αβTCRs in an individual (Arstila et al., 1999; Davis and Bjorkman, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Individual TCR transcripts can be used as endogenous cellular barcodes inherited by the T cell progeny.
source: Due to this diversity, the individual TCR transcripts can be used as endogenous cellular barcodes inherited by the T cell progeny.
evidence: This is an inference based on TCR diversity and is supported by the cited applications.

claim: TCR diversity has been utilized for providing quantitative insight into TCR diversity.
source: This has been utilized for providing quantitative insight into TCR diversity (Robins et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: TCR diversity has been used to trace lineage decisions of T cells.
source: to trace lineage decisions of T cells (Gerlach et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: TCR diversity has been used to monitor the dynamics of T cells across immune-related diseases, such as infectious disease, cancer and autoimmunity.
source: and to monitor the dynamics of T cells across immune-related diseases, such as infectious disease (Dziubianau et al., 2013; Hou et al., 2016), cancer (Kirsch et al., 2015; Sherwood, 2013; Zhang et al., 2018) and autoimmunity (Acha-Orbea et al., 1988; Madi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Most TCR repertoire studies have been confined to bulk experiments, tracing the TCR β chain because of its greater diversity compared to the alpha chain.
source: Most of such TCR repertoire studies have been confined to bulk experiments, tracing the TCR β chain because of its greater diversity (compared to the alpha chain) and because it is less ambiguous due to allelic exclusion (Bergman, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents established practice in the field.

claim: Accurate pairing of the variable TCR α and β regions is valuable for uncovering the biological function of a T cell.
source: However, accurate pairing of the variable TCR α and β regions is valuable for uncovering the biological function of a T cell and is generally lost in bulk experiments since the transcripts are separately encoded.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of bulk sequencing and the importance of paired chain information.

claim: Paired α and β TCR data are essential for the characterization and learning of the relationship between the TCR sequence and specificity.
source: Moreover, we and others have earlier demonstrated that paired α and β TCR data are essential for the characterization and learning of the relationship between the TCR sequence and specificity (Montemurro et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors and others.

claim: Single-cell sequencing platforms can be applied to simultaneously capture both TCR chains while retaining cell origin information.
source: To accurately obtain TCR αβ-sequence-pair, single-cell sequencing platforms can be applied to simultaneously capture both TCR chains, while retaining cell origin information.
evidence: This describes the capability of single-cell sequencing platforms, which is established technology.

claim: T cells can be stained with barcode-labeled pMHC multimers to simultaneously identify pMHC specificity and TCR sequence of individual cells.
source: To further assign specificity information to such TCRs, T cells can be stained with barcode-labeled pMHC multimers to simultaneously identify pMHC specificity and TCR sequence of individual cells (Bentzen et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The platform facilitates screening of surface proteins via DNA barcoded antibodies to distinguish cellular subtypes and enables cell hashing.
source: Moreover, via DNA barcoded antibodies, the platform facilitates screening of surface proteins to distinguish cellular subtypes and enables cell hashing to trace origin of a given cell to, for example, a given donor, sample, or time point, which is highly valuable in patient studies.
evidence: This describes technical capabilities of the platform used in the study.

claim: Single-cell sequencing was applied to describe T cell specificities toward a set of viral-derived peptide-MHC (pMHC) complexes.
source: Here we thus applied single-cell sequencing to describe the T cell specificities toward a set of viral-derived peptide-MHC (pMHC) complexes.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: The pMHCs were selected to expand current knowledge of TCR-pMHC interactions and covered pMHCs with limited or no paired TCR coverage in public-domain databases such as IEDB and VDJdb.
source: The pMHCs were selected with the purpose of generating data to expand the current knowledge of TCR-pMHC interactions, and hence covered pMHCs with limited or no paired TCR coverage in the public-domain databases such as IEDB (Vita et al., 2019) and VDJdb (Bagaev et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the rationale for pMHC selection in the study.

claim: The droplet-based single-cell platform from 10x Genomics was deployed.
source: We deployed the droplet-based single-cell platform from 10x Genomics.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the technology used.

claim: Ideally a droplet contains a single cell with all its analytes and a gel-bead in emulsion (GEM).
source: Ideally a droplet contains a single cell with all its analytes and a gel-bead in emulsion (GEM).
evidence: This describes the ideal operation of the 10x Genomics platform.

claim: The gel-bead contains barcoded primers that ensure tracing of transcripts back to the cell of origin, referred to as GEMs.
source: The gel-bead contains barcoded primers that ensures tracing of transcripts back to the cell of origin, referred to as GEMs.
evidence: This describes the technical mechanism of the 10x Genomics platform.

claim: The sequence deconvolution is associated with substantial noise and is challenging to discriminate true from false signals.
source: While the platform is highly promising, the sequence deconvolution is associated with substantial noise, and challenging to discriminate true from false signals.
evidence: This is supported by the detailed analysis of noise sources presented in the manuscript.

claim: Common confounding factors include stochastic gene expression, cell cycle variations, apoptosis, and technical artifacts such as multiplet capture, contamination, dropout, and batch effects.
source: Common confounding factors include stochastic gene expression, cell cycle variations, apoptosis, and technical artifacts such as multiplet capture, contamination, dropout, and batch effects.
evidence: This is established knowledge about single-cell sequencing challenges.

claim: Dropout and stochastic gene expression both result in zero-inflated gene counts and are typically insensitive to low expression levels.
source: Dropout and stochastic gene expression both result in zero-inflated gene counts and are typically insensitive to low expression levels (Buettner et al., 2015; Kharchenko et al., 2014; Yamawaki et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Multiplet capture is the event of capturing two or more cells in a single GEM, and it is proportional to the capture rate of cells introduced to the system.
source: Multiplet capture is the event of capturing two or more cells in a single GEM, and it is proportional to the capture rate of cells introduced to the system (Bloom, 2018; Zheng et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: To include even low-frequency cell populations, the capture rate must be high at the expense of introducing more multiplets.
source: Thus, to include even low-frequency cell populations, the capture rate must be high at the expense of introducing more multiplets.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between capture rate and multiplet formation.

claim: Contamination is particularly an issue when including analytes such as pMHC multimers, which may be dissolved in cell suspension.
source: Contamination is particularly an issue when including analytes such as pMHC multimers, which may be dissolved in cell suspension (Gaublomme et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation and observed in the data presented.

claim: The platform has no means of controlling how ambient analytes and their barcodes are partitioned with GEMs, which leads to GEMs that appear like multiplets or consist of ambiguous annotations from multiple analyte barcodes.
source: The platform has no means of controlling how ambient analytes and their barcodes are partitioned with GEMs, which leads to GEMs that appear like multiplets or consist of ambiguous annotations from multiple analyte barcodes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the technical limitations of the platform and supported by the data showing contamination.

claim: Analytes may dissociate from the cell before capture.
source: The reverse issue arises from the risk that analytes may dissociate from the cell before capture.
evidence: This is a speculation about a potential source of error in the platform.

claim: The main concerns when screening for TCR specificity are nonspecific binding of pMHC and/or cell hashing analytes, incomplete TCR annotation, and T cell multiplets.
source: The main concerns when screening for TCR specificity are nonspecific binding of pMHC and/or cell hashing analytes, incomplete TCR annotation, and T cell multiplets.
evidence: This is based on the analysis of the data and represents the key challenges addressed by ITRAP.

claim: Nonspecific binding and T cell multiplets may completely dilute the signal from actual interactions.
source: Nonspecific binding and T cell multiplets may completely dilute the signal from actual interactions, while incomplete TCRs that are missing the annotation for either α- or β-chain render the single-cell setup superfluous.
evidence: This is an inference about the impact of these confounding factors on data quality.

claim: A data-driven algorithm was developed that facilitates a consistent and reproducible TCR categorization (clonotyping), peptide-MHC (pMHC) annotation, and antibody-based cell hashing referencing of the donors and their HLA profile.
source: To ensure that a screening is fully exploited and interpreted correctly, we set out to develop a data-driven algorithm that facilitates a consistent and reproducible TCR categorization (clonotyping), peptide-MHC (pMHC) annotation, and antibody-based cell hashing referencing of the donors and their HLA profile.
evidence: This describes the main contribution of the paper, which is the ITRAP algorithm.

claim: The algorithm was applied to a dataset derived from screening PBMCs from 16 healthy donors for T cell recognition against common viruses.
source: We applied this algorithm to a dataset derived from screening PBMCs from 16 healthy donors for T cell recognition against common viruses.
evidence: This describes the experimental validation of the algorithm.

claim: A total of 10 different pMHC multimers were evaluated for TCR recognition, each labeled with a unique barcode.
source: In total, we evaluated TCR recognition against 10 different pMHC multimers, each labeled with their unique barcode.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design.

claim: Following the filtering steps described, a confident pairing of pMHC specificity and TCR sequence can be obtained.
source: We demonstrate that following the filtering steps described here we can obtain a confident pairing of pMHC specificity and TCR sequence.
evidence: This is supported by the performance metrics and validation presented in the Results section.

claim: This strategy will open novel opportunities to evaluate the structural interplay and the sequence-driven signatures of pMHC recognition at large scale.
source: This strategy will open novel opportunities to evaluate the structural interplay and the sequence-driven signatures of pMHC recognition at large scale.
evidence: This is a speculation about the future applications of the method.

claim: All samples were stained with the same panel composed of 10 different viral-derived pMHC multimers, each labeled with a unique barcode for that specificity and a common fluorescent label (allophycocyanin [APC]).
source: All samples were stained with the same panel composed of 10 different viral-derived pMHC multimers, each labeled with a unique barcode for that specificity and a common fluorescent label (allophycocyanin [APC]) (Figure 1; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental staining protocol and is shown in Figure 1.

claim: Cells were co-stained with the three most commonly reported viral-derived pMHC multimers (all A0201 restricted: GLC, GIL, NLV) bearing a different fluorochrome (phycoerythrin [PE]) and labeled with their own unique DNA barcode.
source: We wished to enrich only for TCRs responsive to less commonly reported pMHCs, hence we co-stained the cells with the three most commonly reported viral-derived pMHC multimers (all A0201 restricted: GLC, GIL, NLV) bearing a different fluorochrome (phycoerythrin [PE]) and labeled with their own unique DNA barcode (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental design for negative controls.

claim: Only the APC-labeled pMHC multimer binding T cells were sorted and included in the downstream single-cell processing.
source: We sorted only the APC-labeled pMHC multimer binding T cells (and hence deselected the PE-labeled T cells) and included these in the downstream single-cell processing.
evidence: This describes the cell sorting strategy.

claim: Each sample was stained with a distinct hashing antibody to provide a sample identification barcode associated with the GEMs of the resultant single-cell data set.
source: Prior to sorting, each sample was stained with a distinct hashing antibody to provide a sample identification barcode associated with the GEMs of the resultant single-cell data set.
evidence: This describes the cell hashing protocol used in the study.

claim: Cell hashing enables mixing of cells from different samples while retaining the information of sample origin.
source: This is done to enable mixing of cells from different samples, while retaining the information of sample origin, and utilizing the capacity of capturing 6000–10,000 cells per lane in the 10x Genomics workflow.
evidence: This describes the purpose and benefit of cell hashing.

claim: The MHC multimer-positive population is generally of low frequency (<1% of CD8 T cells).
source: This is essential when capturing T cells based on their specificity since the MHC multimer-positive population is generally of low frequency (<1% of CD8 T cells).
evidence: This is established knowledge about antigen-specific T cell frequencies.

claim: When several samples are mixed in the process of running the single-cell analysis, all mRNA and DNA barcodes associated with a given cell will be encoded with the same 10x barcode, proving the GEM association.
source: When several samples are mixed in the process of running the single-cell analysis, all mRNA and DNA barcodes (derived from hashing antibodies or the MHC multimers) associated with a given cell will be encoded with the same 10x barcode, proving the GEM association (Figure 1; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes how the 10x platform maintains cell identity through barcoding.

claim: The single-cell data is annotated using 10x Chromium Cellranger multi v6.1.
source: The single-cell data is annotated using 10x Chromium Cellranger multi v6.1.
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics tool used for initial data processing.

claim: Each GEM is quantified by a count of unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) for the three components (TCR, pMHC, and sample hashing) based on transcripts of TCR α- and β-chains, barcodes co-attached to pMHC multimers and barcodes co-attached to cell hashing antibodies.
source: This results in each GEM being quantified by a count of unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) (Kivioja et al., 2011) for the three components (TCR, pMHC, and sample hashing) based on transcripts of TCR α- and β-chains, barcodes co-attached to pMHC multimers and barcodes co-attached to cell hashing antibodies (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the data structure output by the sequencing and annotation pipeline.

claim: A total of 1800 pMHC multimer-positive cells were sorted per donor.
source: To obtain the data presented here, a total of 1800 pMHC multimer-positive cells were sorted per donor irrespective of the frequency or the number of different antigen-specific T cell responses in a given sample, accumulating to a total of 28,800 cells sorted (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design.

claim: All sorted cells were loaded into a single lane for 10x processing.
source: All sorted cells were loaded into a single lane for 10x processing.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure.

claim: Based on experience with pre-sorting of low frequent cell populations, loading 28,800 cells equals a total of 6000–9000 captured cells per lane after running the full 10x Genomics 5′ pipeline, and an acceptable doublet rate.
source: Based on experience with pre-sorting of low frequent cell populations, this equals a total of 6000–9000 captured cells per lane after running the full 10x Genomics 5′ pipeline, and an acceptable doublet rate.
evidence: This is based on prior experience with the platform.

claim: Initially, each GEM was annotated based on the most abundant transcripts from TCRαβ, pMHC, and cell hashing.
source: Initially, each GEM was annotated based on the most abundant transcripts from TCRαβ, pMHC, and cell hashing.
evidence: This describes the initial annotation approach.

claim: Annotating based on most abundant transcripts can lead to erroneous annotations as the noise level can differ substantially for the different reagents, resulting in different levels of UMIs.
source: However, this can lead to erroneous annotations as the noise level can differ substantially for the different reagents, resulting in different levels of UMIs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of variable noise levels in the data.

claim: Based on raw, unfiltered data, 6073 GEMs contained all three components (TCR, pMHC, and sample hashing), corresponding to 40% of the loaded cells.
source: Based on raw, unfiltered data, we found 6073 GEMs that contained all three components, that is, TCR, pMHC, and sample hashing, corresponding to 40% of the loaded cells (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis shown in Figure 2a.

claim: A total of 716,069 GEMs only contained one or two of the components, with the majority containing only the cell hashing barcode (n = 677,502).
source: A total of 716,069 GEMs only contained one or two of the components, with the majority containing only the cell hashing barcode (n = 677,502) and the second largest share containing cell hashing as well as pMHC barcodes (n = 37,277).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: The number of GEMs with incomplete components vastly exceeds the number of cells in the assay (15,700 cells loaded) and indicates contamination from ambient barcodes in suspension.
source: This number vastly exceeds the number of cells in the assay (15,700 cells loaded) and indicates contamination from ambient barcodes in suspension.
evidence: This is an inference based on the discrepancy between expected and observed GEM counts.

claim: The sample hashing UMI count was significantly higher (p<0.0005, Mann–Whitney U) in the 6073 GEMs containing a TCR compared to the GEMs void of TCR.
source: This is further supported by the observation that the sample hashing UMI count was significantly higher (p<0.0005, Mann–Whitney U) in the 6073 GEMs containing a TCR compared to the GEMs void of TCR (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis shown in Figure 2b.

claim: A total of 43,455 GEMs captured a DNA barcode associated with the pMHC library and only 14% of these were completed with TCR transcripts and sample hashing barcodes.
source: A total of 43,455 GEMs captured a DNA barcode associated with the pMHC library and only 14% of these were completed with TCR transcripts and sample hashing barcodes.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: In the GEMs containing a TCR, 84% were completed with all three components (hashing and pMHC barcodes).
source: In the GEMs containing a TCR, 84% were completed with all three components, that is, included hashing and pMHC barcodes, while less than 0.05% of these GEMs were void of both sample hashing and pMHC barcodes.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: The high degree of noise also affects the 6073 GEMs containing all three components.
source: In the following, we will only consider the 6073 GEMs containing all three components, while taking into account that the high degree of noise also affects these seemingly completely mapped GEMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of noise in the data.

claim: Without further filtering, the pMHC-TCR pairing is subjected to extensive noise.
source: Without further filtering, the pMHC-TCR pairing is subjected to extensive noise (Figure 2d)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2d showing the noisy data before filtering.

claim: All 10 DNA barcodes associated with the APC-labeled pMHCs were captured in a varying number of GEMs.
source: and we capture all the 10 DNA barcodes associated with the APC-labeled pMHCs in a varying number of GEMs.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the data.

claim: The three negative control responses (GIL A0201, GLC A0201, and NLV A0201) are only captured in a few GEMs as the most abundant pMHC (GIL: 4 GEMs/clonotypes; GLC: 17 GEMs/clonotypes; and NLV: 12 GEMs/clonotypes).
source: Importantly, the three negative control responses (GIL A0201, GLC A0201, and NLV A0201), which were present in the donors but not sorted, are only captured in a few GEMs; both as the most abundant pMHC (GIL: 4 GEMs/clonotypes; GLC: 17 GEMs/clonotypes; and NLV: 12 GEMs/clonotypes)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: The vast majority (84%) of the negative control pMHCs had UMI counts of 1 when present as presumed contamination.
source: and as presumed contamination (i.e., examples where the UMI count of the negative control(s) was not the most abundant). In this latter case, the vast majority (84%) of the negative control pMHCs had UMI counts of 1.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: Four of the abundant negative control responses matched known IEDB/VDJdb responses.
source: Four of the abundant negative control responses matched known IEDB/VDJdb responses.
evidence: This is a result from cross-referencing the data with public databases.

claim: The cell isolation via sorting is effective in terms of capturing only the desired cells and relevant pMHC-associated barcode labels.
source: This indicates that the cell isolation via sorting is effective in terms of capturing only the desired cells and relevant pMHC-associated barcode labels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the low detection of negative control pMHCs.

claim: The most frequently detected pMHC across all GEMs is RVR A0301, which is present with high UMI counts across all GEMs.
source: The most frequently detected pMHC across all GEMs is RVR A0301, which is present with high UMI counts across all GEMs.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Only RPH(10-mer) B0702-associated UMIs was consistently detected at low numbers per GEM.
source: Only RPH(10-mer) B0702-associated UMIs was consistently detected at low numbers per GEM.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the data.

claim: Mismatches between pMHC HLA and donor HLA are typically found in GEMs where the most abundant pMHC is detected at low UMI counts while the matches consist of GEMs with higher pMHC UMI counts.
source: Typically, the mismatches are found in GEMs where the most abundant pMHC is detected at low UMI counts while the matches consist of GEMs with higher pMHC UMI counts.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Of the 65% GEMs containing pMHC multiplets, 13% contained two or more pMHCs at the exact same UMI level.
source: Of the 65% GEMs containing pMHC multiplets (Figure 2c), 13% contained two or more pMHCs at the exact same UMI level (Supplementary file 3), which may either represent noise or true cross-binding events.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: Based on the unfiltered data, five TCR-pMHC matches (across nine GEMs) were found in IEDB and VDJdb databases.
source: The detected specificities in our data have been cross-referenced with the IEDB (Vita et al., 2019) and VDJdb (Bagaev et al., 2020) databases (Figure 2d). Based on the unfiltered data, we found five TCR-pMHC matches (across nine GEMs)
evidence: This is a result from cross-referencing the data with public databases.

claim: One TCR (one GEM) was annotated with a different pMHC than registered in IEDB and VDJdb.
source: and one TCR (one GEM), which was annotated with a different pMHC (Figure 2d). This latter is a case of a GEM with multiple pMHCs present with almost equal number of UMIs, where the most abundant pMHC is RVR A0301 (11 UMIs) and the second most abundant pMHC is GLC A0201 (9 UMIs), which is the peptide registered as target in IEDB and VDJdb.
evidence: This is a specific example from the data analysis.

claim: Most of the captured T cells interact with several of the screened pMHCs to a degree that exceeds the level expected from natural cross-recognition.
source: The data in Figure 2d suggests that most of the captured T cells interact with several of the screened pMHCs to a degree that exceeds the level expected from natural cross-recognition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of multiple pMHC signals per GEM.

claim: It is reasonable to assume that a large proportion of pMHC multiplets are formed as a result of ambient pMHC leaking into GEMs.
source: Therefore, it is reasonable to assume that a large proportion of these multiplets are formed as a result of ambient pMHC leaking into GEMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of extensive multiplets and known contamination issues.

claim: A substantial part of the data consists of noise (GEMs with multiplets of pMHC and sample hashing) and must be filtered for proper interpretation.
source: From these observations, it is clear that a substantial part of the data consists of noise, that is, GEMs with multiplets of pMHC and sample hashing, and that the data must be filtered for proper interpretation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data analysis presented.

claim: Initial clonotypes were called using 10x Genomics Cellranger, which defines a clonotype as a set of cells that share identical receptor sequences at the nucleotide level, spanning the entirety of the V(D)J-C genes as well as the junction segments.
source: Initial clonotypes were called using 10x Genomics Cellranger, which defines a clonotype as a set of cells that share identical receptor sequences at the nucleotide level, spanning the entirety of the V(D)J-C genes as well as the junction segments.
evidence: This describes the clonotype definition used by the Cellranger software.

claim: Clonotypes were redefined based on TCR annotation, with GEMs annotated to existing clonotypes conditioned on matching VJαβ-genes and CDR3αβ sequences or as novel clonotypes.
source: Assuming reliable gene and CDR3 sequence calls by 10x Cellranger, we redefine clonotypes based on TCR annotation. Subsequently, GEMs with no clonotype annotation from 10x were annotated to existing clonotypes conditioned on matching VJαβ-genes and CDR3αβ sequences or as novel clonotypes.
evidence: This describes the clonotype annotation approach used in ITRAP.

claim: Clonotypes with identical VJ-CDR3αβ were merged to form larger groups of theoretically identical TCRs.
source: Similarly, clonotypes with identical VJ-CDR3αβ were merged to form larger groups of theoretically identical TCRs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the clonotype merging approach used in ITRAP.

claim: Merging GEMs of the same TCR is essential to make statistical inference based on those groupings, for example, determine expected pMHC target per clonotype.
source: Merging GEMs of the same TCR is essential to make statistical inference based on those groupings, for example, determine expected pMHC target per clonotype.
evidence: This is a rationale for the clonotype merging approach.

claim: The outcome was a set of 2441 TCR clonotypes across the 6073 GEMs containing both TCR and pMHC.
source: The outcome was a set of 2441 TCR clonotypes across the 6073 GEMs containing both TCR and pMHC.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clonotype annotation.

claim: For the 337 GEMs containing TCR chain multiplets, the most abundant chain per GEM was selected to represent the true TCR.
source: For the 337 GEMs containing TCR chain multiplets, the most abundant chain per GEM was for the subsequent analyses selected to represent the true TCR.
evidence: This describes a data processing decision made in the analysis.

claim: Not all GEMs within a given clonotype support the same pMHC target.
source: As we have seen earlier, not all GEMs within a given clonotype support the same pMHC target, and defining the pMHC target of a TCR based on individual GEMs thus results in contradicting annotations.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis.

claim: The key to identify the expected target for a clonotype is to determine which pMHC identity represents the majority of UMIs across all GEMs within a given clonotype.
source: The key to identify the expected target for a clonotype is therefore to determine which pMHC identity represents the majority of UMIs across all GEMs within a given clonotype.
evidence: This is a key principle of the ITRAP method.

claim: Figure 3 illustrates an example from a pilot study that accentuates the importance of studying GEMs in ensemble rather than individually.
source: Figure 3 illustrates an example from a pilot study that accentuates the importance of studying GEMs in ensemble rather than individually.

claim: A fraction of clonotype singlets likely represents nonspecific binding events.
source: This likely reflects that a fraction of such clonotype singlets represents nonspecific binding events.

claim: Removing clonotype singlets as a standard procedure of ITRAP results in a substantial loss of TCR capture, represented by all T cell specificities with a light gray outer circle in Figure 7b.

claim: The UMI thresholds identified by ITRAP are data specific and cannot be universally applied but must be fitted for individual experiments.

claim: The ITRAP method was capable of accurately denoising the 10x Genomics public data set.
source: In short, we find that the ITRAP method also for this data set was capable of accurately denoising the raw data.

claim: The accuracy of ITRAP on the 10x Genomics public data set was manifested through highly improved internal performance metric values and improved predictive power of a NetTCR machine learning method trained on the denoised data.
source: This accuracy was manifested not only through highly improved internal performance (concordance, accuracy, and AUC) metric values, but also in improved predictive power of a NetTCR (Montemurro et al., 2022) machine learning method trained on the denoised data.
evidence: This is a result from the additional validation study.

claim: Due to very different experimental settings in the two data sets, the obtained UMI-based filtering thresholds varied between the two studies.
source: Due to the very different experimental settings in the two data sets, the obtained UMI-based filtering thresholds as expected varied between the two studies.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the two studies.

claim: The variation in optimal thresholds between studies indicates the high strength of ITRAP being robust at being applied to data generated in very different biological and technical settings.
source: This indicates the high strength of ITRAP being robust at being applied to data generated in very different biological and technical settings.

claim: ITRAP performance was benchmarked against ICON (Integrative COntext-specific Normalization).
source: Other than investigating the robustness of ITRAP, the paper also benchmarked ITRAP performance against ICON (Integrative COntext-specific Normalization) (Zhang et al., 2021).

claim: ICON was developed for denoising and discriminating true TCR-pMHC binding signal from nonspecific background noise in single-cell data.

source: The results from this benchmark suggested an overall superior performance of the ITRAP method compared with the ICON method in terms of both data consistency and performance.
evidence: This is a result from the benchmark comparison.

source: One clonotype may display natural low affinity toward its cognate target, which might appear like noise in the comparison to other high-affinity clonotypes.

source: This diversity in signals is challenging to handle in a one-fit-all filtering process, and for projects with specific interest in low-affinity cell interactions, a specific focus should be addressed not to lose such information.
